assumptions.obligation: i_full_thr is static: it does not change while both domains are out of hardware reset.
i_empty_thr is static: it does not change while both domains are out of hardware reset.
No write (i_wr_en=0) while either hardware reset is asserted.
No read (i_rd_en=0) while either hardware reset is asserted.
i_rst_n_wr is released only at a rising edge of i_clk_wr (synchronous release, low for at least one write-clock edge). Assertion stays asynchronous.
i_rst_n_rd is released only at a rising edge of i_clk_rd (synchronous release, low for at least one read-clock edge). Assertion stays asynchronous.
After one domain's hardware reset, no write until the other domain has also been reset and both are released. The resets need not be simultaneous.
After one domain's hardware reset, no read until the other domain has also been reset and both are released. The resets need not be simultaneous.

notes:
CHK-002, CHK-004, CHK-010, CHK-011, CHK-012: each comes from a reset pulse released between clock edges, so no edge ever sampled it low. The specification obliges synchronous release with at least one clock edge low (AF-6.2-03, AF-3-34, AF-20.1-01). ENV-05 and ENV-06 add this. Releasing only at a rising edge also gives the minimum width, because the releasing edge samples the reset low. Reset assertion stays asynchronous and unconstrained (AF-7.3-01, AF-7.3-02, AF-7.3-07).

CHK-003, CHK-013: each needs a hardware reset of one domain followed by traffic. AF-12-07 obliges the integrator to reset both domains, and AF-7.2-12 / AF-20.2-27 say the IP does not repair a one-sided reset. ENV-07 and ENV-08 block traffic from the moment one domain is reset until the other has also been reset and both are released. The two resets may still come at different times and need not overlap (AF-3-36, AF-7.2-11).

Choice to review: pairing is required always, not only after an accepted access, because AF-12-07 is unconditional. The weaker form gated by 'FIFO used' was considered and not chosen.

Not added because the specification does not oblige it: (1) A flush wait of S edges after the second of two non-overlapping resets. A synchronizer can still hold an old pointer for S edges after that reset. If a counterexample appears in that window, raise it as a gap in the specification. (2) Any constraint on i_rst_n_sw during a one-sided reset (AF-6.2-11, AF-7.3-07 allow it at any time).
